transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... well, I hope it's okay that I'm here. I don't want to be a bother or take up too much of your time. I guess I'm just feeling really worn down lately. For about a year now, I've been... well, I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or, um, holding back parts of my dad's lab results. 

I know how that sounds, I really do, and I don't want to seem difficult or anything. My family and all the doctors keep telling me the numbers are perfectly fine. But... I know the chart doesn't match what I actually saw. It's just been really exhausting trying to get people to see it, and it's really wearing me down. 

I'm sorry, does that make sense? I just didn't know where else to go.

When you think about these lab results, do you feel like you are being forced to think about them against your will, or do you feel like you are choosing to pursue this because you are certain your observation is accurate?

Oh, um... no, it's not like I'm being forced. I definitely don't feel like the thoughts are out of my control or anything like that. I really don't want you to think I'm... well, I'm completely in control of my own head, I promise. 

I guess... I guess I'm choosing to pursue it. Just because I'm so sure of what I saw. Working as a phlebotomist, I see these kinds of lab results all the time, so I know what to look for, you know? I just want to make sure my dad gets the right care. That's a normal thing to want for your family, right? 

I really hope I don't sound too stubborn or difficult by keeping at it. I'm just trying to do the right thing as his daughter... is that okay?
Aside from your concerns regarding the lab results, have you noticed anything else unusual or suspicious occurring in your daily life?

Um... no, not really. Aside from the whole thing with the lab results, everything else is just... normal. Just my regular life. I go to work, I come home, I try to take care of my dad. 

I haven't noticed anything else suspicious or weird at all. I mean, I'm a pretty reasonable person, you know? I don't go looking for conspiracies or anything like that. I really hope you don't think I'm the type of person who just imagines things are wrong everywhere. It's really just this one specific thing with the chart because I know what I saw. 

Everything else is perfectly fine. I promise I'm not, like, paranoid about my whole life. Does that make sense? I just want to be clear that I'm functioning totally fine otherwise.
Do you believe that the people at the clinic are intentionally trying to harm your father or interfere with his medical care?

Um... no, no, I don't think they're trying to hurt him. I really don't. I mean, I know doctors and nurses work really hard, and I'd never want to accuse anyone of, like, intentionally trying to cause harm. That would be awful, right? 

I just... I think maybe it's just a mistake, or someone is covering up a mistake so they don't get in trouble. You know how people can get defensive if they do something wrong at work? I think it's more like that. Just someone trying to hide an error with the paperwork. 

I definitely don't think there's some big, evil plot to hurt my dad. I hope I didn't make it sound that way before. I really respect the medical field—I mean, I work in it! I just want the chart to be accurate. That's a reasonable way to look at it, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not coming across as, well, crazy or accusatory.
Have you ever heard any voices or sounds that other people around you couldn't hear?

Oh, goodness, no. No, definitely not. I've never heard voices or... or any sounds that aren't really there. I know that's probably a standard question you have to ask everybody, but I promise I don't have anything like that going on. 

I really want to assure you that my mind is completely clear. I know sometimes people who are... well, going through severe mental health things might hear voices, but that's absolutely not me. I'm just a regular person who happened to catch a paperwork error at the clinic, you know? 

I really hope you don't think I'm losing touch with reality or anything like that. I'm totally grounded. It's a good sign that I don't hear anything like that, right? I just want to make sure you know I'm doing okay and that I'm being helpful.

Aside from the situation with your father's medical records, have you ever felt that you possess any special knowledge, unique talents, or a specific mission that others around you do not seem to recognize or understand?

Oh, my gosh, no. No, definitely not. I don't have any kind of secret mission or... or special powers or anything like that. I'm really just a regular person. I mean, I'm a phlebotomist, and I try to be really good at my job, but that's just from practice and hard work, you know? Not some unique, magical talent. 

I really hope I haven't said anything that made you think I'm arrogant or... or full of myself. I'd hate for you to think I'm one of those people who thinks they're better or more important than everyone else. I just want to live a quiet life, go to work, and make sure my dad is taken care of. 

That's a totally normal way to be, isn't it? I really just want you to see that I'm completely down-to-earth and realistic. I'm answering these okay, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need and being as helpful as possible.
When you have discussed these concerns with the doctors and shown them the evidence you have, how do you explain their continued insistence that the lab results are correct?

Um... well, it's really hard, actually. I try to be so polite when I bring it up, because I know they're busy, but... I mean, for the past year, I've just been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or, you know, holding back parts of my dad's lab results. 

And I know how it sounds, I really do. I know it sounds like I'm being difficult. And no matter how many doctors or even my own family members tell me the numbers are fine, I just... I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. I saw it with my own eyes. 

I don't want to be a bother, and I hate arguing with people who have medical degrees. It just makes me feel terrible. But it's wearing me down so much. I just want someone to look at the evidence I have and say, 'Oh, you're right, let's fix this.' 

I guess... I guess I just explain their insistence by thinking they're too busy to really look closely, or maybe they just trust the system too much to believe it could be wrong. I really hope I'm not coming across as stubborn or unreasonable. I'm just trying to do the right thing for my dad, you know? That makes sense, doesn't it? I just want to be a good daughter.

Do you feel that the doctors or staff have ever acted in a way that suggests they are personally targeting you or trying to keep you from the truth for reasons other than just being busy or making a mistake?

Oh, no, no, I don't think they're targeting me personally. I mean, I really don't want to sound like one of those paranoid people who thinks everyone is out to get them. I know the doctors are good people, and I'm sure they got into medicine to help people, just like I try to help people when I draw their blood. 

I don't think it's a... a conspiracy against me or anything scary like that. I really just think it's a paperwork thing, or maybe they just don't want to admit a mistake was made because of liability? That happens in healthcare sometimes, right? 

I really try to be respectful of their time and their expertise. I'd never want them to think I'm accusing them of something malicious. I just want the records fixed for my dad. That's a completely reasonable way to look at it, don't you think? I really hope I'm being clear and not sounding like I'm trying to cause trouble for anyone. I'm just trying to be helpful and honest with you.
Are there any other people, besides yourself, who have personally looked at these lab results and agreed with you that they have been altered or are incorrect?

Um... well... no. Not exactly. I mean, I've tried to show my family, but they just... they don't really understand medical charts, you know? They just kind of glance at it and trust whatever the front desk tells them. And I haven't really shown anyone at my work because I don't want to be unprofessional and bring my personal family issues into the clinic. 

So... I guess, no, there isn't really anyone else who has sat down and agreed with me about it. 

I know how that sounds. I really do. I'm so worried it makes me sound like I'm just being difficult or... or making things up, and I promise you I'm not. It's just that, since I do blood draws every day, I'm kind of the only one in my family who really knows what these specific lab printouts are supposed to look like. So it makes sense that I'd be the only one to catch the mistakes, right? 

I really hope you don't think less of me because I'm the only one pushing for this. I'm just trying to be as thorough as I can for my dad's sake. I'm answering all of this okay, aren't I? I just want to be completely open with you so you can see I'm really just trying to do the right thing.

When you are speaking with these doctors about your concerns, do you find that you have any difficulty keeping your thoughts organized or that your mind feels like it is jumping from one topic to another?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um... I actually try to be really, really careful about how I explain things to them. I know they're so busy, so I always make sure I have my thoughts completely organized before I even bring it up. 

My mind doesn't jump around or anything like that. I just stay very focused on the specific lab values that I know were changed. I'd hate for them to think I'm just... you know, rambling or being overly emotional. I want to be as professional and respectful of their time as possible. 

I haven't seemed disorganized while we've been talking today, have I? I really try my best to be clear. It's just so important to me that I communicate this the right way, so you can see I'm just trying to be a good advocate for my dad. I hope I'm doing okay explaining it all to you.
How has this year-long struggle to correct these records affected your ability to maintain your daily responsibilities at work and at home?

Oh, it hasn't affected my daily life like that at all. Um, I really want to make sure you know that I'm completely on top of things. Outside of the... the whole dispute about my dad's records, I still keep all my phlebotomy shifts. I haven't missed work or anything, I promise. I pay my bills on time, I take care of myself, and I just manage all my normal day-to-day responsibilities without any problems.

I'd never let something like this make me neglect my job or my life. I know how important it is to be reliable, especially working in a clinic. I really don't want you to think I'm falling apart or... or obsessing in a way that ruins my life, because I'm really not. I'm doing a good job keeping everything normal and balanced, don't you think? I really hope you can see that I'm still a very responsible person who just wants to get a clerical error fixed.
